evidence: Additive after 0084: no table, column, policy, function, grant, permission, control or applied migration is removed or rewritten, and runtime-grants.sql does not change. 0085 inserts one row into identity.purpose_of_use_codes, ('emergency', 'Emergency treatment', active, source 'hid'), with ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING, exactly as main's 0097 section 2 and this branch's 0071 (direct-care) do: a row an operator already inserted or deactivated is kept as it is and never reactivated. The code at the previous release keeps working on the new schema: it reads purpose codes only through activation, standard access requests, PIN grants and has_active_consent_grant, and with the row active the previous Identity's break-glass, which does not check the control, also succeeds for the holders of identity.break-glass.write (doctor, clinician and nurse since 0010), both during the rollout (0085 commits before the new Identity serves) and after any rollback to the previous Identity (the schema stays). That matches the owner's decision of 2026-10-24 to enable break-glass now (accepting no staff MFA and main's other launch limits) only while break_glass_enabled is on, so reading GET /admin/controls and confirming break_glass_enabled is on is a precondition of merging; if it is off, the release waits for the owner.The new Identity checks platform.require_control_enabled('break_glass_enabled') inside the activation transaction (423 BREAK_GLASS_DISABLED when off, 503 PLATFORM_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE when unreadable) and answers a missing or inactive emergency purpose 423 instead of 400; break_glass_enabled is not changed (0039 seeded it on). Locks until commit: ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.purpose_of_use_codes and its primary key index only, measured with pg_locks on PostgreSQL 16 (under 1 ms); the table has no row-level security, policy, rule or user trigger, and its only triggers are the referencing foreign keys' action triggers, which fire on UPDATE and DELETE, never INSERT, so no reader or writer of any table waits. No NOTICE for an inactive existing row: the runner's node-postgres client discards notices; the post-deploy check is the read-only query in 0085's header. Built 0001-0085 on PostgreSQL 16 in production order (0001-0072, role bootstrap with the 0072-era runtime-grants.sql, then 0073-0085), the same followed by a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql, and in new-installation order (0001-0085, then role bootstrap); the migration plan and dry run on a 0084 database list and apply only 0085; every suite in services/ehr-api/database/tests (emergency.integration.sql included, whose own emergency fixture insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and services/ehr-api/test/database passes in each, and the database/tests suites the rehearsal runs, with the emergency-contacts and new suites, pass under a non-superuser, NOBYPASSRLS definer owner. The synthetic migration rehearsal (scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs, run as a non-root user on PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector) passes: its 0028-to-0085 upgrade keeps every historical purpose row and finds exactly the active direct-care and emergency rows its migrations declare.The new suite test/database/break-glass-launch.integration.sql fails at 0084 and passes at 0085; through the exact Identity runtime role and a doctor's staff context without platform.control.read it shows the control check passing, the grant, approved request, audit row and EmergencyAccessActivated outbox row written, 0084's trigger creating exactly one intent (one verified contact with alerts on among three), the audited admin command turning the control off making the check raise 55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_DISABLED:break_glass_enabled with nothing written, and an operator-deactivated emergency row refusing activation with 22023 and staying exactly as it was when 0085 runs again; it catches each of 11 deliberate defects in 0085.
